candidates.rationale: The implementation inspects the first IPv6 segment, but vstd has no logical view connecting Ipv6Addr to its segments or octets.
risks: An exact predicate requires a new Ipv6Addr representation abstraction.

candidates.rationale: The source compares the address bytes with UNSPECIFIED, but neither the byte representation nor the associated constant has an existing vstd model.
risks: Using opaque equality or an unmodeled constant would not establish the source-level byte semantics.

candidates.rationale: A useful constructor contract must relate the result to its eight segments or sixteen octets, for which no Ipv6Addr view exists in vstd.
risks: Specifying the result through other unmodeled Ipv6Addr methods would be circular.

candidates.rationale: The method exposes a private byte field, and current vstd provides no public logical representation of an Ipv6Addr against which to specify the returned array.
risks: A deterministic postcondition would require inventing a representation view or referencing private state.

candidates.rationale: The returned native-endian segments are derived from the private octets, but no existing vstd abstraction connects an Ipv6Addr to either representation.
risks: Encoding the endian conversion requires a new Ipv6Addr logical view.

candidates.rationale: The result is the big-endian interpretation of the private octets, which cannot be related to the opaque address using current vstd vocabulary.
risks: An exact bit-level contract requires a modeled octet or numeric view of Ipv6Addr.
